appDescription: A demanding inland-to-coast stage from Mörtfors to Stjärneberg. The route leaves the Mörtfors cabin, follows Marströmmen, crosses E22 near Solstadström, reaches the Baltic at Hålviken, then continues through Kallsebo, Snäckedal, Arvidsmåla and the Trollklinten area before roads toward Adriansnäs and the Misterhult-Klintemåla road lead to Stjärneberg. Use repaired official geometry rather than raw GPX, and carry Stjärneberg cabin/well availability as a publication-time check rather than a static closure.

camping: Mörtfors cabin/tenting is a standard official Ostkustleden overnight option and shared with Etapp 4.
Current official Stjärneberg cabin text checked on 2026-04-29 does not show the earlier bed-bug closure claim; model cabin/tenting availability as publication-time information.
Misterhults skärgård reserve rules matter only if leaving the main route for nearby islands/waters; camping in reserve context is limited to one night in the same place.
fire: Mörtfors cabin has no fireplaces and no fires are permitted outside the cabin.
Stjärneberg has indoor iron stove/fireplace as facility metadata, but no outside fires at the cottage.
Fire-ban feed showed no Oskarshamn fire ban at access time, but SMHI fire-risk warnings were active/high to very high for Kalmar mainland April 29-May 1, 2026; recheck same day.
Do not light fires at the slightest fire danger per maintainer/reserve safety context.
toilets: Mörtfors toilet beside the house is high-confidence but needs duplicate handling with Etapp 4 records.
Stjärneberg dry toilet remains available but exact separate coordinate was not found.

closuresAndReroutes.notes: No current trail closure, reroute or forestry-operation notice found in searched official/currentness sources. Follow-up checks of the current Stjärneberg Naturkartan page and maintainer pages on 2026-04-29 did not reproduce the earlier bed-bug closure or arsenic wording; treat cabin and well availability as publication-time checks.

protectedAreas.name: Mörtfors naturreservat / Stora Ramm and Marströmmen Natura 2000 SE0330239
rulesSummary: Applies at the Mörtfors start context.
Permission may be needed for organized/commercial exploitation, surveys/signage, and collecting moss/lichen/fungi except edible fungi.
Dogs should be leashed to protect wildlife/young animals.
Natura 2000 permit may be needed for activities that can affect protected values, even outside the area.

protectedAreas.name: Misterhults skärgård naturreservat / Natura 2000 SE0330049
rulesSummary: If entering reserve islands/waters, dogs/pets must not run loose, wildlife must not be disturbed, camping is limited to one night in the same place, and fire bans restrict fire.
C-areas have seasonal access restrictions: no entry or being within 100 m, and no boat travel within 100 m, from April 1 to July 10.
protectedAreas.notes: Exact GIS intersection with Etapp 5 GPX and any C-areas remains open.

dogs.summary: Maintainer asks dog supervision and leashing at farms/livestock and when meeting others on narrow paths. Swedish law requires dogs to be prevented from running loose where wildlife exists during March 1-August 20.

hunting.summary: Latest official Kalmar elk decision found was for 2025/2026: elk-management/licence areas October 8, 2025-January 31, 2026 and unregistered areas October 8-12, 2025 calf only. That season had ended by the 2026-04-29 access date; 2026/2027 dates were not found.

fire.summary: No Oskarshamn fire ban was shown by the official feed at access time, but SMHI had active high/very-high fire-risk warnings for Kalmar mainland for April 29-May 1, 2026. Cabin rules and same-day fire status should override generic facility fire icons.

waterProtection.summary: Oskarshamn municipality lists protected drinking-water areas Bockara, Kristdala, Fårbo, Hummeln, Djupeträsk, Eckern and Älvehult; Mörtfors, Stjärneberg, Hålviken, Kallsebo, Snäckedal and Arvidsmåla do not appear on that list. This is not a GIS legal-boundary check.

trailSpecificSafety.summary: Be careful crossing E22 near Solstadström. Later section after Snäckedal is hilly/rocky. Field reports add overgrowth, slippery slabs and route-finding caution.

conditionReports.sectionRelevance: Exact Mörtfors to Bussvik outing, including Etapp 5 and part of Etapp 6
conditionReports.summary: Reported Etapp 5 as partly quite overgrown, somewhat messy, with many elevation meters, very little asphalt/gravel, two wrong turns, slippery rock slabs and markings easy to miss when concentrating on footing.

Describes forest paths and gravel roads, Hålviken, rocky/old quarry landscape, and Stjärneberg cabin as usable but in need of care, with kitchen, living room/stove, electricity, mattresses, firewood, toilets and a newer hut with more beds.
conditionReports.notes: Its Hålviken distance conflicts with other descriptions; use only as field/context support and defer Stjärneberg availability to current official/publication-time checks.

conditionReports.summary: Recent route-wide reviews mention good conditions, bugs and low crowding; other reviews warn the trail can be hard to follow and AllTrails linework may be an older version.
conditionReports.notes: Use as general route-following caveat only.

conditionReports.summary: Mörtfors-E22 marked hard physical but easy to follow; E22-Vickerum and Kallseboskogen marked hard and sometimes hard to follow. No useful trail reports posted.
Old personal trip photo confirms Hålviken was used as a swim spot.
conditionReports.notes: Use only as old location context.

sourceContradictions.details: Naturkartan page/API says 21.4 km, official PDF and Döderhult say about 19 km, rules lane found an 18.3 km Naturkartan text variant, OSM says 19 km, Pacer says about 18.5 km, and repaired official GPX is 18.734 km.
sourceContradictions.resolution: Treat 21.4 km as duplicate-geometry artifact and use about 19 km for intended display distance, with repaired official GPX length retained for normalization.

sourceContradictions.details: Official GPX/API includes two duplicate short Mörtfors-side lines and a reversed main line; raw summing creates the 21.4 km distance.
sourceContradictions.resolution: Do not import raw. Discard T2, reverse T1, reverse/trim T3, and join at the shared junction.

sourceContradictions.details: Naturkartan route-page marker 57.5434451248887,16.4808952113779 is about 2.16 km straight-line from the Mörtfors cabin and corresponds to the duplicated GPX junction.
sourceContradictions.resolution: Use cleaned GPX start and Mörtfors cabin marker for endpoint metadata; mark page pin as not endpoint.

sourceContradictions.details: The original Etapp 5 synthesis recorded a closure/bed-bug notice, while Etapp 6 lanes and a direct follow-up check of the current Stjärneberg Naturkartan page on 2026-04-29 did not reproduce any visible closure notice.
sourceContradictions.resolution: Do not mark Stjärneberg closed from the candidate data. Import as a cabin cluster only with a publication-time availability check before user-facing overnight claims.

sourceContradictions.details: The original Etapp 5 synthesis recorded an arsenic warning, while Etapp 6 lanes and a direct follow-up check of the current Stjärneberg Naturkartan page on 2026-04-29 found boil-water wording only.
sourceContradictions.resolution: Use boil-water/currentness wording from current official text. Do not import the well as an unqualified potable-water point and do not carry a static arsenic warning without a reproducible source.

sourceContradictions.details: Snäckedal is an official POI on/near the trail, but Länsstyrelsen says car visitors cannot currently be directed there due to no access-road/parking agreement.
sourceContradictions.resolution: Import as on-foot cultural POI, not as car access/parking.
